L239@P2: algorithm for PEPS contraction, and compare it to other
L240@P2: methods. Indeed, we first used the BP algorithm as a
L241@P2: contraction subroutine in an imaginary time evolution

L244@P2: be explained theoretically; the mean field approximation
L245@P2: at the heart of the simple-update method and the BP
L246@P2: algorithm are equivalent.
L247@P2: III. THE SIMPLE UPDATE METHOD
L248@P2: The simple-update method [27] is a direct generalization of the TEBD [28–30] algorithm for 1D real and imaginary times evolution to higher dimensions. It calculates
L249@P2: the dynamics of many-body spin systems that sit on a
L250@P2: lattice, and are described by a (quasi-) canonical PEPS
L251@P2: tensor-network. The method is efficient and numerically
L252@P2: stable, but often results in poor accuracy due to its oversimplified representation of local environments.
L253@P2: At its core lies a quasi-canonical form of the PEPS
L254@P2: that allows a crude approximation of local TN environments. This approximation is often referred to as mean
L255@P2: field approximation. When the PEPS is in the shape
L256@P2: of a tree, this form is truly canonical: it corresponds to
L257@P2: consecutive Schmidt decompositions of the many-body
L258@P2: quantum state. Every edge in the graph connects two
L259@P2: disjoint branches of the system, which correspond to
L260@P2: the Schmidt decomposition between these two branches
L261@P2: |ψi =

L264@P2: |Lii ⊗ |Rii. Specifically, the TN consists
L265@P2: of two types of tensors: tensors Ta that are connected
L266@P2: to the physical legs, and diagonal λ tensors that sit in
L267@P2: the middle of every edge and correspond to the Schmidt
L268@P2: weights, as illustrated in Fig. 3. The orthonormality of
L269@P2: the Schmidt decomposition, and its correspondence with
L270@P2: the TN structure implies that contraction over branches
L271@P2: of the tree is given by a simple Kronecker delta function
L272@P2: (Fig. 3b). Therefore, the RDMs of a given region can be
L273@P2: readily computed using only the tensors that surround it
L274@P2: (Fig. 3c), and in addition the tensors must satisfy local
L275@P2: canonical conditions shown in (Fig. 3b). This type of
L276@P2: approximation is often referred to as mean field approximation of the environment in the TN literature.
L277@P2: When the underlying graph has loops, the canonical
L278@P2: form is no longer well-defined; removing an edge from
L279@P2: the graph no longer divides it into two parts, and so it
L280@P2: cannot be associated with a Schmidt decomposition between two branches. Nevertheless, we can still define a
L281@P2: PEPS to be quasi-canonical if it satisfies the local canonical constraints of Fig. 3b2. In such case, the expression
L282@P2: for local RDMs (e.g., Fig. 3c) is no longer exact. Nevertheless, when the graph looks locally like a tree, or when
L283@P2: the quantum state has only short-range correlations, this
L284@P2: approximation is often reasonable.
